items.text: I watched a man in a Carhartt jacket put back a gallon of milk at the gas station because the total at the pump had already eaten what he came in with. He didn't argue. He just nodded at the clerk like they'd already had the conversation a hundred times. I was standing two people behind him, holding a bag of dog food and a quart of motor oil for our Buick, and I watched him slide that milk back into the cooler with the kind of care a man uses when he's pretending nothing is wrong. He set it in the same spot. He turned the label so it faced out, the way you'd put a book back on a library shelf. Then he walked out into the lot. He sat in his truck for a long minute before he started the engine. The truck was clean. Older, but clean. A man who took care of his things. I knew that man. I didn't know his name. But I knew him. I'd been married to a version of him for forty-one years. My name is Maggie. I'm sixty-four. I drove a school bus in our county for twenty-six years and I retired last

items.text: Keira stood in front of the Horton Group Headquarters, disguised in a courier uniform. Her heart pounded as she stared at the impossible marriage certificate inside the box. “This is insane, but I have no other choice,” she muttered to herself. She had so many questions. And only one man could answer them all: Lewis Horton, her supposed husband. She swiftly made her way to the boardroom and entered without knocking. Twenty executives in thousand-dollar suits turned as Keira strode in. At the head of the table sat Lewis Horton himself—even more striking in person than in the photograph, with dark hair and piercing eyes. “Mr. Horton,” she said, her voice shaking only slightly. “We need to talk.” Lewis’s gaze flicked over her uniform, then the box. “Who let the courier in during a meeting?” “This isn’t a delivery.” She pulled out the paper, slapping it on the polished table. “It’s a marriage certificate. items.text: 🍍🍗🫑One Pan Hawaiian-Inspired Chicken Ingredients: • 2–3 chicken breasts (or thighs) • 2 bell peppers, sliced • 1 red onion, sliced • 1–2 cups pineapple chunks (fresh or canned, drained) • ½–1 cup teriyaki sauce (I use Primal Kitchen) • Olive oil • Salt, pepper, garlic powder • Cooked rice, for serving Instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 400°F. 2. Add bell peppers, red onion, and pineapple to a large baking dish or sheet pan. 3. Drizzle veggies with olive oil and season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Toss to coat. 4. In a bowl, season chicken with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Pour teriyaki sauce over the chicken and toss until coated. 5. Place chicken on top of the veggies. 6. Bake uncovered for 25–30 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (165°F). 7. Optional: Broil for 2–3 minutes at the end for a little caramelization. 8. Serve over rice and spoon extra juices from the pan on top. And be sure to download the @recime.app to download this recipe & more straight to your pho
